NKJV.1: I am the man who has seen affliction by the rod of His wrath.
NKJV.2: He has led me and made me walk In darkness and not in light.
NKJV.3: Surely He has turned His hand against me Time and time again throughout the day.
NKJV.4: He has aged my flesh and my skin, And broken my bones.
NKJV.5: He has besieged me And surrounded me with bitterness and woe.
NKJV.6: He has set me in dark places Like the dead of long ago.
NKJV.7: He has hedged me in so that I cannot get out; He has made my chain heavy.
NKJV.8: Even when I cry and shout, He shuts out my prayer.
NKJV.9: He has blocked my ways with hewn stone; He has made my paths crooked.
NKJV.10: He has been to me a bear lying in wait, Like a lion in ambush.
NKJV.11: He has turned aside my ways and torn me in pieces; He has made me desolate.
NKJV.12: He has bent His bow And set me up as a target for the arrow.
NKJV.13: He has caused the arrows of His quiver To pierce my loins.
NKJV.14: I have become the ridicule of all my people—  Their taunting song all the day.
NKJV.15: He has filled me with bitterness, He has made me drink wormwood.
NKJV.16: He has also broken my teeth with gravel, And covered me with ashes.
NKJV.17: You have moved my soul far from peace; I have forgotten prosperity.
NKJV.18: And I said, “My strength and my hope Have perished from the LORD.”
NKJV.19: Remember my affliction and roaming,  The wormwood and the gall.
NKJV.20: My soul still remembers And sinks within me.
NKJV.21: This I recall to my mind, Therefore I have hope.
NKJV.22: Through the LORD’s mercies we are not consumed, Because His compassions fail not.
NKJV.23: They are new every morning; Great is Your faithfulness.
NKJV.24: “The LORD is my portion,” says my soul, “Therefore I hope in Him!”
NKJV.25: The LORD is good to those who wait for Him, To the soul who seeks Him.
NKJV.26: It is good that one should hope and wait quietly For the salvation of the LORD.
NKJV.27: It is good for a man to bear The yoke in his youth.
NKJV.28: Let him sit alone and keep silent, Because God has laid it on him;
NKJV.29: Let him put his mouth in the dust— There may yet be hope.
NKJV.30: Let him give his cheek to the one who strikes him, And be full of reproach.
NKJV.31: For the Lord will not cast off forever.
NKJV.32: Though He causes grief, Yet He will show compassion According to the multitude of His mercies.
NKJV.33: For He does not afflict willingly, Nor grieve the children of men.
NKJV.34: To crush under one’s feet All the prisoners of the earth,
NKJV.35: To turn aside the justice due a man Before the face of the Most High,
NKJV.36: Or subvert a man in his cause—  The Lord does not approve.
NKJV.37: Who is he who speaks and it comes to pass, When the Lord has not commanded it?
NKJV.38: Is it not from the mouth of the Most High That woe and well-being proceed?
NKJV.39: Why should a living man complain,  A man for the punishment of his sins?
NKJV.40: Let us search out and examine our ways, And turn back to the LORD;
NKJV.41: Let us lift our hearts and hands To God in heaven.
NKJV.42: We have transgressed and rebelled; You have not pardoned.
NKJV.43: You have covered Yourself with anger And pursued us; You have slain and not pitied.
NKJV.44: You have covered Yourself with a cloud, That prayer should not pass through.
NKJV.45: You have made us an offscouring and refuse In the midst of the peoples.
NKJV.46: All our enemies Have opened their mouths against us.
NKJV.47: Fear and a snare have come upon us,  Desolation and destruction.
NKJV.48: My eyes overflow with rivers of water For the destruction of the daughter of my people.
NKJV.49: My eyes flow and do not cease, Without interruption,
NKJV.50: Till the LORD from heaven  Looks down and sees.
NKJV.51: My eyes bring suffering to my soul Because of all the daughters of my city.
NKJV.52: My enemies without cause Hunted me down like a bird.
NKJV.53: They silenced my life in the pit And threw stones at me.
NKJV.54: The waters flowed over my head;  I said, “I am cut off!”
NKJV.55: I called on Your name, O LORD, From the lowest pit.
NKJV.56: You have heard my voice: “Do not hide Your ear From my sighing, from my cry for help.”
NKJV.57: You drew near on the day I called on You, And said, “Do not fear!”
NKJV.58: O Lord, You have pleaded the case for my soul;  You have redeemed my life.
NKJV.59: O LORD, You have seen how I am wronged; Judge my case.
NKJV.60: You have seen all their vengeance, All their schemes against me.
NKJV.61: You have heard their reproach, O LORD, All their schemes against me,
NKJV.62: The lips of my enemies And their whispering against me all the day.
NKJV.63: Look at their sitting down and their rising up; I am their taunting song.
NKJV.64: Repay them, O LORD, According to the work of their hands.
NKJV.65: Give them a veiled heart; Your curse be upon them!
NKJV.66: In Your anger, Pursue and destroy them  From under the heavens of the LORD.

NASB.1: I am the man who has seen affliction Because of the rod of His wrath.
NASB.2: He has driven me and made me walk In darkness and not in light.
NASB.3: Surely against me He has turned His hand Repeatedly all the day.
NASB.4: He has caused my flesh and my skin to waste away, He has broken my bones.
NASB.5: He has besieged and encompassed me with bitterness and hardship.
NASB.6: In dark places He has made me dwell, Like those who have long been dead.
NASB.7: He has walled me in so that I cannot go out; He has made my chain heavy.
NASB.8: Even when I cry out and call for help, He shuts out my prayer.
NASB.9: He has blocked my ways with hewn stone; He has made my paths crooked.
NASB.10: He is to me like a bear lying in wait, [Like] a lion in secret places.
NASB.11: He has turned aside my ways and torn me to pieces; He has made me desolate.
NASB.12: He bent His bow And set me as a target for the arrow.
NASB.13: He made the arrows of His quiver To enter into my inward parts.
NASB.14: I have become a laughingstock to all my people, Their [mocking] song all the day.
NASB.15: He has filled me with bitterness, He has made me drunk with wormwood.
NASB.16: He has broken my teeth with gravel; He has made me cower in the dust.
NASB.17: My soul has been rejected from peace; I have forgotten happiness.
NASB.18: So I say, 'My strength has perished, And [so has] my hope from the LORD.'
NASB.19: Remember my affliction and my wandering, the wormwood and bitterness.
NASB.20: Surely my soul remembers And is bowed down within me.
NASB.21: This I recall to my mind, Therefore I have hope.
NASB.22: The LORD'S lovingkindnesses indeed never cease, For His compassions never fail.
NASB.23: [They] are new every morning; Great is Your faithfulness.
NASB.24: 'The LORD is my portion,' says my soul, 'Therefore I have hope in Him.'
NASB.25: The LORD is good to those who wait for Him, To the person who seeks Him.
NASB.26: [It is] good that he waits silently For the salvation of the LORD.
NASB.27: [It is] good for a man that he should bear The yoke in his youth.
NASB.28: Let him sit alone and be silent Since He has laid [it] on him.
NASB.29: Let him put his mouth in the dust, Perhaps there is hope.
NASB.30: Let him give his cheek to the smiter, Let him be filled with reproach.
NASB.31: For the Lord will not reject forever,
NASB.32: For if He causes grief, Then He will have compassion According to His abundant lovingkindness.
NASB.33: For He does not afflict willingly Or grieve the sons of men.
NASB.34: To crush under His feet All the prisoners of the land,
NASB.35: To deprive a man of justice In the presence of the Most High,
NASB.36: To defraud a man in his lawsuit-- Of these things the Lord does not approve.
NASB.37: Who is there who speaks and it comes to pass, Unless the Lord has commanded [it]?
NASB.38: [Is it] not from the mouth of the Most High That both good and ill go forth?
NASB.39: Why should [any] living mortal, or [any] man, Offer complaint in view of his sins?
NASB.40: Let us examine and probe our ways, And let us return to the LORD.
NASB.41: We lift up our heart and hands Toward God in heaven;
NASB.42: We have transgressed and rebelled, You have not pardoned.
NASB.43: You have covered [Yourself] with anger And pursued us; You have slain [and] have not spared.
NASB.44: You have covered Yourself with a cloud So that no prayer can pass through.
NASB.45: [You have made us mere] offscouring and refuse In the midst of the peoples.
NASB.46: All our enemies have opened their mouths against us.
NASB.47: Panic and pitfall have befallen us, Devastation and destruction;
NASB.48: My eyes run down with streams of water Because of the destruction of the daughter of my people.
NASB.49: My eyes pour down unceasingly, Without stopping,
NASB.50: Until the LORD looks down And sees from heaven.
NASB.51: My eyes bring pain to my soul Because of all the daughters of my city.
NASB.52: My enemies without cause Hunted me down like a bird;
NASB.53: They have silenced me in the pit And have placed a stone on me.
NASB.54: Waters flowed over my head; I said, 'I am cut off!'
NASB.55: I called on Your name, O LORD, Out of the lowest pit.
NASB.56: You have heard my voice, 'Do not hide Your ear from my [prayer for] relief, From my cry for help.'
NASB.57: You drew near when I called on You; You said, 'Do not fear!'
NASB.58: O Lord, You have pleaded my soul's cause; You have redeemed my life.
NASB.59: O LORD, You have seen my oppression; Judge my case.
NASB.60: You have seen all their vengeance, All their schemes against me.
NASB.61: You have heard their reproach, O LORD, All their schemes against me.
NASB.62: The lips of my assailants and their whispering [Are] against me all day long.
NASB.63: Look on their sitting and their rising; I am their mocking song.
NASB.64: You will recompense them, O LORD, According to the work of their hands.
NASB.65: You will give them hardness of heart, Your curse will be on them.
NASB.66: You will pursue them in anger and destroy them From under the heavens of the LORD!

NLT.1:
I am the one who has seen the afflictions
that come from the rod of the LORD’s anger.
NLT.2:
He has led me into darkness,
shutting out all light.
NLT.3:
He has turned his hand against me
again and again, all day long.
NLT.4:
He has made my skin and flesh grow old.
He has broken my bones.
NLT.5:
He has besieged and surrounded me
with anguish and distress.
NLT.6:
He has buried me in a dark place,
like those long dead.
NLT.7:
He has walled me in, and I cannot escape.
He has bound me in heavy chains.
NLT.8:
And though I cry and shout,
he has shut out my prayers.
NLT.9:
He has blocked my way with a high stone wall;
he has made my road crooked.
NLT.10:
He has hidden like a bear or a lion,
waiting to attack me.
NLT.11:
He has dragged me off the path and torn me in pieces,
leaving me helpless and devastated.
NLT.12:
He has drawn his bow
and made me the target for his arrows.
NLT.13:
He shot his arrows
deep into my heart.
NLT.14:
My own people laugh at me.
All day long they sing their mocking songs.
NLT.15:
He has filled me with bitterness
and given me a bitter cup of sorrow to drink.
NLT.16:
He has made me chew on gravel.
He has rolled me in the dust.
NLT.17:
Peace has been stripped away,
and I have forgotten what prosperity is.
NLT.18:
I cry out, “My splendor is gone!
Everything I had hoped for from the LORD is lost!”
NLT.19:
The thought of my suffering and homelessness
is bitter beyond words.
NLT.20:
I will never forget this awful time,
as I grieve over my loss.
NLT.21:
Yet I still dare to hope
when I remember this:
NLT.22:
The faithful love of the LORD never ends!
His mercies never cease.
NLT.23:
Great is his faithfulness;
his mercies begin afresh each morning.
NLT.24:
I say to myself, “The LORD is my inheritance;
therefore, I will hope in him!”
NLT.25:
The LORD is good to those who depend on him,
to those who search for him.
NLT.26:
So it is good to wait quietly
for salvation from the LORD.
NLT.27:
And it is good for people to submit at an early age
to the yoke of his discipline:
NLT.28:
Let them sit alone in silence
beneath the LORD’s demands.
NLT.29:
Let them lie face down in the dust,
for there may be hope at last.
NLT.30:
Let them turn the other cheek to those who strike them
and accept the insults of their enemies.
NLT.31:
For no one is abandoned
by the Lord forever.
NLT.32:
Though he brings grief, he also shows compassion
because of the greatness of his unfailing love.
NLT.33:
For he does not enjoy hurting people
or causing them sorrow.
NLT.34:
If people crush underfoot
all the prisoners of the land,
NLT.35:
if they deprive others of their rights
in defiance of the Most High,
NLT.36:
if they twist justice in the courts —
doesn’t the Lord see all these things?
NLT.37:
Who can command things to happen
without the Lord’s permission?
NLT.38:
Does not the Most High
send both calamity and good?
NLT.39:
Then why should we, mere humans, complain
when we are punished for our sins?
NLT.40:
Instead, let us test and examine our ways.
Let us turn back to the LORD.
NLT.41:
Let us lift our hearts and hands
to God in heaven and say,
NLT.42:
“We have sinned and rebelled,
and you have not forgiven us.
NLT.43:
“You have engulfed us with your anger, chased us down,
and slaughtered us without mercy.
NLT.44:
You have hidden yourself in a cloud
so our prayers cannot reach you.
NLT.45:
You have discarded us as refuse and garbage
among the nations.
NLT.46:
“All our enemies
have spoken out against us.
NLT.47:
We are filled with fear,
for we are trapped, devastated, and ruined.”
NLT.48:
Tears stream from my eyes
because of the destruction of my people!
NLT.49:
My tears flow endlessly;
they will not stop
NLT.50:
until the LORD looks down
from heaven and sees.
NLT.51:
My heart is breaking
over the fate of all the women of Jerusalem.
NLT.52:
My enemies, whom I have never harmed,
hunted me down like a bird.
NLT.53:
They threw me into a pit
and dropped stones on me.
NLT.54:
The water rose over my head,
and I cried out, “This is the end!”
NLT.55:
But I called on your name, LORD,
from deep within the pit.
NLT.56:
You heard me when I cried, “Listen to my pleading!
Hear my cry for help!”
NLT.57:
Yes, you came when I called;
you told me, “Do not fear.”
NLT.58:
Lord, you have come to my defense;
you have redeemed my life.
NLT.59:
You have seen the wrong they have done to me, LORD.
Be my judge, and prove me right.
NLT.60:
You have seen the vengeful plots
my enemies have laid against me.
NLT.61:
LORD, you have heard the vile names they call me.
You know all about the plans they have made.
NLT.62:
My enemies whisper and mutter
as they plot against me all day long.
NLT.63:
Look at them! Whether they sit or stand,
I am the object of their mocking songs.
NLT.64:
Pay them back, LORD,
for all the evil they have done.
NLT.65:
Give them hard and stubborn hearts,
and then let your curse fall on them!
NLT.66:
Chase them down in your anger,
destroying them beneath the LORD’s heavens.

WEB.1: I am the man that has seen affliction by the rod of his wrath.
WEB.2: He has led me and caused me to walk in darkness, and not in light.
WEB.3: Surely against me he turns his hand again and again all day long.
WEB.4: He has made my flesh and my skin old; he has broken my bones.
WEB.5: He has built against me, and surrounded me with gall and travail.
WEB.6: He has made me to dwell in dark places, as those that have been long dead.
WEB.7: He has walled me about, that I can’t go out; he has made my chain heavy.
WEB.8: Yes, when I cry, and call for help, he shuts out my prayer.
WEB.9: He has walled up my ways with cut stone; he has made my paths crooked.
WEB.10: He is to me as a bear lying in wait, as a lion in secret places.
WEB.11: He has turned aside my ways, and pulled me in pieces; he has made me desolate.
WEB.12: He has bent his bow, and set me as a mark for the arrow.
WEB.13: He has caused the shafts of his quiver to enter into my kidneys.
WEB.14: I have become a derision to all my people, and their song all day long.
WEB.15: He has filled me with bitterness. He has sated me with wormwood.
WEB.16: He has also broken my teeth with gravel stones; he has covered me with ashes.
WEB.17: You have removed my soul far off from peace; I forgot prosperity.
WEB.18: I said, “My strength has perished, along with my expectation from Yahweh.”
WEB.19: Remember my affliction and my misery, the wormwood and the gall.
WEB.20: My soul still remembers them, and is bowed down within me.
WEB.21: This I recall to my mind; therefore I have hope.
WEB.22: It is because of Yahweh’s loving kindnesses that we are not consumed, because his compassion doesn’t fail.
WEB.23: They are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
WEB.24: “Yahweh is my portion,” says my soul. “Therefore I will hope in him.”
WEB.25: Yahweh is good to those who wait for him, to the soul who seeks him.
WEB.26: It is good that a man should hope and quietly wait for the salvation of Yahweh.
WEB.27: It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth.
WEB.28: Let him sit alone and keep silence, because he has laid it on him.
WEB.29: Let him put his mouth in the dust, if so be there may be hope.
WEB.30: Let him give his cheek to him who strikes him; let him be filled full with reproach.
WEB.31: For the Lord will not cast off forever.
WEB.32: For though he cause grief, yet he will have compassion according to the multitude of his loving kindnesses.
WEB.33: For he does not afflict willingly, nor grieve the children of men.
WEB.34: To crush under foot all the prisoners of the earth,
WEB.35: To turn aside the right of a man before the face of the Most High,
WEB.36: To subvert a man in his cause, the Lord doesn’t approve.
WEB.37: Who is he who says, and it comes to pass, when the Lord doesn’t command it?
WEB.38: Doesn’t evil and good come out of the mouth of the Most High?
WEB.39: Why does a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins?
WEB.40: Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to Yahweh.
WEB.41: Let us lift up our heart with our hands to God  in the heavens.

WEB.58: Lord, you have pleaded the causes of my soul; you have redeemed my life.

WEB.65: You will give them hardness of heart, your curse to them.

AMP.1:
I am [Jeremiah] the man who has seen affliction
Because of the rod of His wrath.
AMP.2:
He has led me and made me walk
In darkness and not in light.
AMP.3:
Surely He has turned His hand against me
Repeatedly all the day.
AMP.4:
He has caused my flesh and my skin to waste away;
He has shattered my bones.
AMP.5: He has besieged and surrounded me with bitterness and hardship.
AMP.6:
He has made me live in dark places
Like those who have long been dead.
AMP.7:
He walled me in so that I cannot get out;
He has weighted down my chain.
AMP.8:
Even when I cry out and shout for help,
He shuts out my prayer.
AMP.9:
He has blocked my ways with cut stone;
He has made my paths crooked.
AMP.10:
He is to me like a bear lying in wait,
And like a lion [hiding] in secret places.
AMP.11:
He has turned aside my ways and torn me in pieces;
He has made me desolate.
AMP.12:
He has bent His bow
And set me as a target for the arrow.
AMP.13:
He has caused the arrows of His quiver
To enter my inner parts.
AMP.14:
I have become the [object of] ridicule to all my people,
And [the subject of] their mocking song all the day.
AMP.15:
He has filled me with bitterness;
He has made me drunk with wormwood (bitterness).
AMP.16:
He has broken my teeth with gravel;
He has [covered me with ashes and] made me cower in the dust.
AMP.17:
My soul has been cast far away from peace;
I have forgotten happiness.
AMP.18:
So I say, "My strength has perished
And so has my hope and expectation from the LORD."
AMP.19: Remember [O LORD] my affliction and my wandering, the wormwood and the gall (bitterness).
AMP.20:
My soul continually remembers them
And is bowed down within me.
AMP.21:
But this I call to mind,
Therefore I have hope.
AMP.22:
It is because of the Lord's lovingkindnesses that we are not consumed,
Because His [tender] compassions never fail.
AMP.23:
They are new every morning;
Great and beyond measure is Your faithfulness.
AMP.24:
"The LORD is my portion and my inheritance," says my soul;
"Therefore I have hope in Him and wait expectantly for Him."
AMP.25:
The LORD is good to those who wait [confidently] for Him,
To those who seek Him [on the authority of God's word].
AMP.26:
It is good that one waits quietly
For the salvation of the LORD.
AMP.27:
It is good for a man that he should bear
The yoke [of godly discipline] in his youth.
AMP.28:
Let him sit alone [in hope] and keep quiet,
Because God has laid it on him [for his benefit].
AMP.29:
Let him put his mouth in the dust [in recognition of his unworthiness];
There may yet be hope.
AMP.30:
Let him give his cheek to the one who strikes him;
Let him be filled with reproach.
AMP.31: For the Lord will not reject forever,
AMP.32:
For if He causes grief,
Then He will have compassion
According to His abundant lovingkindness and tender mercy.
AMP.33:
For He does not afflict willingly and from His heart
Or grieve the children of men.
AMP.34:
To trample and crush under His feet
All the prisoners of the land,
AMP.35:
To deprive a man of justice
In the presence of the Most High,
AMP.36:
To defraud a man in his lawsuit—
The Lord does not approve of these things.
AMP.37:
Who is there who speaks and it comes to pass,
Unless the Lord has authorized and commanded it?
AMP.38:
Is it not from the mouth of the Most High
That both adversity (misfortune) and good (prosperity, happiness) proceed?
AMP.39:
Why should any living mortal, or any man,
Complain [of punishment] in view of his sins?
AMP.40:
Let us test and examine our ways,
And let us return to the LORD.
AMP.41:
Let us lift up our hearts and our hands [in prayer]
Toward God in heaven;
AMP.42:
We have transgressed and rebelled,
You have not pardoned.
AMP.43:
You have covered Yourself with anger
And pursued us;
You have slain [without pity] and have not spared.
AMP.44:
You have covered Yourself with a cloud
So that no prayer can pass through.
AMP.45:
You have made us scum and refuse
Among the peoples (Gentile nations).
AMP.46: All our enemies have gaped at us.
AMP.47:
Panic and pitfall (traps, danger) have come on us,
Devastation and destruction.
AMP.48:
My eyes overflow with streams of tears
Because of the destruction of the daughter of my people (Jerusalem).
AMP.50:
Until the LORD looks down
And sees from heaven.
AMP.51:
My eyes [see things that] bring pain to my soul
Because of all the daughters of my city.
AMP.52:
Without cause my enemies
Hunted me down like a bird;
AMP.53:
They silenced me in the pit
And placed a stone over me.
AMP.54:
The waters ran down on my head;
I said, "I am cut off (destroyed)!"
AMP.55:
I called on Your name, O LORD,
Out of the lowest pit.
AMP.56:
You have heard my voice,
"Do not hide Your ear from my prayer for relief,
From my cry for help."
AMP.57:
You drew near on the day I called to You;
You said, "Do not fear."
AMP.58:
O Lord, You have pleaded my soul's cause [You have guided my way and protected me];
You have rescued and redeemed my life.
AMP.59:
O LORD, You have seen the wrong [done to me];
Judge my case.
AMP.60:
You have seen all their vengeance,
All their schemes against me.
AMP.61:
You have heard their reproach, O LORD,
And all their schemes against me.
AMP.62:
The lips and whispering of my assailants
Are against me all day long.
AMP.63:
Look at their sitting and their rising [their actions and secret counsels];
I am their mocking song [the subject of their ridicule].
AMP.64:
You will repay them, O LORD,
According to the work of their hands.
AMP.65:
You will harden their hearts;
Your curse will be upon them.
AMP.66:
You will pursue them in anger and destroy them
From under the heavens of the LORD.

over and over and over again.

poured on the trouble and hard times.

like a corpse nailed inside a coffin.

manacles my hands, shackles my feet.

a lion in hiding ready to pounce.
MSG.11:
He knocked me from the path and ripped me to pieces.
When he finished, there was nothing left of me.
MSG.12:
He took out his bow and arrows
and used me for target practice.
MSG.13:
He shot me in the stomach
with arrows from his quiver.
MSG.14:
Everyone took me for a joke,
made me the butt of their mocking ballads.
MSG.15:
He forced rotten, stinking food down my throat,
bloated me with vile drinks.
MSG.16:
He ground my face into the gravel.
He pounded me into the mud.
MSG.17:
I gave up on life altogether.
I've forgotten what the good life is like.
MSG.18:
I said to myself, "This is it. I'm finished.
God is a lost cause."
MSG.19:
I'll never forget the trouble, the utter lostness,
the taste of ashes, the poison I've swallowed.
MSG.20:
I remember it all—oh, how well I remember—
the feeling of hitting the bottom.
MSG.21:
But there's one other thing I remember,
and remembering, I keep a grip on hope:
MSG.22:
God's loyal love couldn't have run out,
his merciful love couldn't have dried up.
MSG.23:
They're created new every morning.
How great your faithfulness!
MSG.24:
I'm sticking with God (I say it over and over).
He's all I've got left.
MSG.25:
God proves to be good to the man who passionately waits,
to the woman who diligently seeks.
MSG.26:
It's a good thing to quietly hope,
quietly hope for help from God.
MSG.27:
It's a good thing when you're young
to stick it out through the hard times.
MSG.28:
When life is heavy and hard to take,
go off by yourself. Enter the silence.
MSG.29:
Bow in prayer. Don't ask questions:
Wait for hope to appear.
MSG.30:
Don't run from trouble. Take it full-face.
The "worst" is never the worst.
MSG.31:
Why? Because the Master won't ever
walk out and fail to return.
MSG.32:
If he works severely, he also works tenderly.
His stockpiles of loyal love are immense.
MSG.33:
He takes no pleasure in making life hard,
in throwing roadblocks in the way:
MSG.35:
Refusing justice to victims
in the court of High God,
MSG.36:
Tampering with evidence—
the Master does not approve of such things.
MSG.37:
Who do you think "spoke and it happened"?
It's the Master who gives such orders.
MSG.38:
Doesn't the High God speak everything,
good things and hard things alike, into being?
MSG.39:
And why would anyone gifted with life
complain when punished for sin?
MSG.40:
Let's take a good look at the way we're living
and reorder our lives under God.
MSG.41:
Let's lift our hearts and hands at one and the same time,
praying to God in heaven:
MSG.42:
"We've been contrary and willful,
and you haven't forgiven.
MSG.43:
"You lost your temper with us, holding nothing back.
You chased us and cut us down without mercy.
MSG.44:
You wrapped yourself in thick blankets of clouds
so no prayers could get through.
MSG.45:
You treated us like dirty dishwater,
threw us out in the backyard of the nations.
MSG.46:
"Our enemies shout abuse,
their mouths full of derision, spitting invective.
MSG.47:
We've been to hell and back.
We've nowhere to turn, nowhere to go.
MSG.48:
Rivers of tears pour from my eyes
at the smashup of my dear people.
MSG.49:
"The tears stream from my eyes,
an artesian well of tears,
MSG.50:
Until you, God, look down from on high,
look and see my tears.
MSG.51:
When I see what's happened to the young women in the city,
the pain breaks my heart.
MSG.52:
"Enemies with no reason to be enemies
hunted me down like a bird.
MSG.53:
They threw me into a pit,
then pelted me with stones.
MSG.54:
Then the rains came and filled the pit.
The water rose over my head. I said, 'It's all over.'
MSG.55:
"I called out your name, O God,
called from the bottom of the pit.
MSG.56:
You listened when I called out, 'Don't shut your ears!
Get me out of here! Save me!'
MSG.57:
You came close when I called out.
You said, 'It's going to be all right.'
MSG.58:
"You took my side, Master;
you brought me back alive!
MSG.59:
God, you saw the wrongs heaped on me.
Give me my day in court!
MSG.60:
Yes, you saw their mean-minded schemes,
their plots to destroy me.
MSG.61:
"You heard, God, their vicious gossip,
their behind-my-back plots to ruin me.
MSG.62:
They never quit, these enemies of mine, dreaming up mischief,
hatching out malice, day after day after day.
MSG.63:
Sitting down or standing up—just look at them!—
they mock me with vulgar doggerel.
MSG.64:
"Make them pay for what they've done, God.
Give them their just deserts.
MSG.65:
Break their miserable hearts!
Damn their eyes!
MSG.66:
Get good and angry. Hunt them down.
Make a total demolition here under your heaven!"

You have covered yourself with a cloud

among the nations.
NIV.46:
“All our enemies have opened their mouths
wide against us.
NIV.47:
We have suffered terror and pitfalls,
ruin and destruction.”

Streams of tears flow from my eyes
because my people are destroyed.
NIV.49:
My eyes will flow unceasingly,
without relief,
NIV.50:
until the Lord looks down
from heaven and sees.
NIV.51:

NIV.52:
Those who were my enemies without cause
hunted me like a bird.
NIV.53:
They tried to end my life in a pit

NIV.54:
the waters closed over my head,

NIV.55:
I called on your name, O Lord,
from the depths of the pit.
NIV.56:
You heard my plea: “Do not close your ears
to my cry for relief.”
NIV.57:
You came near when I called you,
and you said, “Do not fear.”
NIV.58:
O Lord, you took up my case;
you redeemed my life.
NIV.59:
You have seen, O Lord, the wrong done to me.
Uphold my cause!
NIV.60:
You have seen the depth of their vengeance,
all their plots against me.
NIV.61:
O Lord, you have heard their insults,

what my enemies whisper and mutter
against me all day long.
NIV.63:
Look at them! Sitting or standing,
they mock me in their songs.
NIV.64:
Pay them back what they deserve, O Lord,
for what their hands have done.
NIV.65:
Put a veil over their hearts,
and may your curse be on them!
NIV.66:
Pursue them in anger and destroy them
from under the heavens of the Lord.
